messages.subject: IMK Stall detected
parts:
Hi

I am relatively new to stan. My model takes about 30 seconds to run for 100 iterations but when I run it for longer it often gets stuck after 100. I get an error message (whilst running it) saying:

 2016-03-31 19:10:54.738 R[813:25271] IMK Stall detected, *please Report* your user scenario in <rdar://problem/16792073> - (imkxpc_attributesForCharacterIndex:reply:) block performed very slowly (1.30 secs)

Sometimes it says up to a minute. I have attached the data. Can anyone tell me what the error means and how to rectify it?

Thanks very much
Mike

The r code is

load('model_outputs.Rdata')

load('stan_problem.Rdata')


getting_arrays<-function(input)

{

outs<-length(input)-2

#output<-array(0,dim=c(outs,input$runs,length(input$Years)))

output<-array(0,dim=c(input$runs,length(input$Years),outs))

for(i in 3:(outs+2))

{

output[,,i-2]<-t(input[[i]])

}

return(output)

}


Miz<-getting_arrays(Mizer)

E2E<-getting_arrays(StrathE2E)

EwE<-getting_arrays(EcoPath)

LeM<-getting_arrays(LeMans)

FiS<-getting_arrays(FishSums)


library(rstan)


EwE_t<-EwE


EwE_t[11,,]<-log10(10^EwE[6,,]+10^EwE[7,,])


M_1<-diag(9)[-c(9),] # Ecopath

M_1[8,9]<-1

M_2<-diag(9)[c(1,2,5,6),] # Mizer

M_3<-diag(9)[c(1,5),] # StrathE2E

M_3[1,c(2,3,4)]<-1

M_3[2,c(5,6,7,8,9)]<-1

M_4<-diag(9)[c(2,5),] # FishSUMS

M_5<-diag(9)[-c(4,9),] # LeMans



beta2<-beta1<-matrix(0,9,9)

for (i in 1:8)

{

for (j in (i+1):9)

{

beta1[i,j]<-beta1[j,i]<-as.numeric(prior[i,j][[1]][1])

beta2[i,j]<-beta2[j,i]<-as.numeric(prior[i,j][[1]][2])

}

}


data.merp<-list(

N=9,time=24,cur=16,

mod_1=8,N_1=EcoPath$runs,y_1=EwE_t[,10:33,c(1,2,8,12,3,4,5,11)],M_1=M_1,# Ecopath

mod_2=4,N_2=Mizer$runs,y_2=Miz[,34:57,],M_2=M_2,# Mizer

mod_3=2,N_3=StrathE2E$runs,y_3=E2E[,18:41,c(2,1)],M_3=M_3,# StrathE2E

mod_4=2,N_4=FishSums$runs,y_4=FiS[,11:34,c(1,2)],M_4=M_4,# FishSUMS

mod_5=7,N_5=LeMans$runs,y_5=LeM[,1:24,c(1,2,7,3,4,5,6)],M_5=M_5,# LeMans

mu_m= margin[,1], mu_v= margin[,2], sig_a= margin[,3], sig_b= margin[,4],

beta1=beta1,beta2=beta2,

Sigma_1=var(EwE_t[,33,c(1,2,8,12,3,4,5,11)]),

Sigma_2=var(Miz[,69,]),

Sigma_3=var(FiS[,46,c(1,2)]),

Sigma_4=var(FiS[,46,c(1,2)]),

Sigma_5=var(LeM[,4,c(1,2,7,3,4,5,6)])

)


fit <- stan(file = 'model_withloops.stan', data = data.merp, 

            iter = 1000, chains = 1,init=0)

            

#########

I am using

R version 3.2.3 (2015-12-10)
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin13.4.0 (64-bit)
Running under: OS X 10.10.5 (Yosemite)

locale:
[1] en_GB.UTF-8/en_GB.UTF-8/en_GB.UTF-8/C/en_GB.UTF-8/en_GB.UTF-8

other attached packages:
[1] rstan_2.9.0-3 ggplot2_2.0.0

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
 [1] colorspace_1.2-6 scales_0.3.0     plyr_1.8.3       tools_3.2.3      inline_0.3.14

[11] munsell_0.4.2    stats4_3.2.3    

########

The stan model is:

functions{
  real As(real Rho){
    real ret;
    ret <- 1/pi() * atan(Rho/sqrt(1-Rho^2))+0.5;
    return ret;
  }
  vector exp10(vector x)
  {
     vector [num_elements(x)] ret;
     for (i in 1:num_elements(x))
     {
        ret[i] <- 10^(x[i]);
     }
     return ret;
  }
  real priors(matrix Rho, int N, matrix beta1, matrix beta2) {
    real log_prior;
    log_prior <- 0;
    for (i in 1:(N-1))  {
      for (j in (i+1):N){
          log_prior <- log_prior + beta_log(As(Rho[i,j]),beta1[i,j],beta2[i,j]);
        }
    }
    return log_prior;
  }
}
data{
  int <lower=0> N; //// Number of variables
  int <lower=0> time;// how long the model is run for
  int <lower=0> cur;// Current year
  // Survey data
  // remove for the time being vector [N] obs [cur]; //Survey data on the log scale 
  // First model
  int<lower=0> mod_1; //// Number of outputs for Model 1
  int<lower=0> N_1; //// Number of observations
  vector [mod_1] y_1[N_1,time]; //// Outputs for Model 1
  matrix [mod_1,N] M_1; //// Matrix of outputs for Model 1
  // Second model
  int<lower=0> mod_2; //// Number of outputs for Model 2
  int<lower=0> N_2; //// Number of observations
  vector [mod_2] y_2[N_2,time]; //// Outputs for Model 2
  matrix [mod_2,N] M_2; //// Matrix of outputs for Model 2
  // Third model
  int<lower=0> mod_3; //// Number of outputs for Model 3
  int<lower=0> N_3; //// Number of observations
  vector [mod_3] y_3[N_3,time]; //// Outputs for Model 3
  matrix [mod_3,N] M_3; //// Matrix of outputs for Model 3
  // Fourth Model
  int<lower=0> mod_4; //// Number of outputs for Model 4
  int<lower=0> N_4; //// Number of observations
  vector [mod_4] y_4[N_4,time]; //// Outputs for Model 4
  matrix [mod_4,N] M_4; //// Matrix of outputs for Model 4
  // Fifth Model
  int<lower=0> mod_5; //// Number of outputs for Model 5
  int<lower=0> N_5; //// Number of observations
  vector [mod_5] y_5[N_5,time]; //// Outputs for Model 5
  matrix [mod_5,N] M_5; //// Matrix of outputs for Model 5
  vector [N] sig_a ; // a for inverse gamma
  vector [N] sig_b ; // b for inverse gamma 
  vector [N] mu_m ; // m for prior mean
  vector [N] mu_v ; // v for prior mean
  matrix [N,N] beta1; // alpha for the prior
  matrix [N,N] beta2; // beta for the prior
  cov_matrix[mod_1] Sigma_1;
  cov_matrix[mod_2] Sigma_2;
  cov_matrix[mod_3] Sigma_3;
  cov_matrix[mod_4] Sigma_4;
  cov_matrix[mod_5] Sigma_5;
}
parameters{
  corr_matrix [N] Rho;
  matrix [N,N] C;
  vector <lower=0> [N] diag_sigma;
  cov_matrix[N] A;
  vector [N] epsilon[time];
  vector [N] x_1[time]; ////truth of Model 1
  vector [N] x_2[time]; ////truth of Model 2
  vector [N] x_3[time]; ////truth of Model 3
  vector [N] x_4[time]; ////truth of Model 4
  vector [N] x_5[time]; ////truth of Model 5
}
transformed parameters{
  cov_matrix [N] Sigma_m;
  matrix [N,N] Sigma_m1;
  matrix [N,N] temp;
  matrix [N,N] temp1;
  vector [N] diag_sigma1;
  vector [mod_1] xx_1[time];
  vector [mod_2] xx_2[time];
  vector [mod_3] xx_3[time];
  vector [mod_4] xx_4[time];
  vector [mod_5] xx_5[time];
  vector [N] mu1[time];
  vector [N] mu2[time];
  vector [N] mu3[time];
  vector [N] mu4[time];
  vector [N] mu5[time];
  cov_matrix [N] Sigma1;
  cov_matrix [N] Sigma2;
  cov_matrix [N] Sigma3;
  cov_matrix [N] Sigma4;
  cov_matrix [N] Sigma5;
  vector [N] mu_prior_var;
  for (i in 1:N)  {
    diag_sigma1[i] <- sqrt(diag_sigma[i]);
    mu_prior_var[i] <- diag_sigma1[i] * sqrt(mu_v[i]);
  }
  Sigma_m<- diag_matrix(diag_sigma1) * Rho * diag_matrix(diag_sigma1);
  Sigma_m1<-inverse_spd(Sigma_m);
  temp<-C' * Sigma_m1 ;
  temp1<-temp * C;
  for (t in (cur+1):time)
  {
    mu1[t] <- epsilon[t]+temp*(x_1[t-1]-epsilon[t-1]);
    mu2[t] <- epsilon[t]+temp*(x_2[t-1]-epsilon[t-1]);
    mu3[t] <- epsilon[t]+temp*(x_3[t-1]-epsilon[t-1]);
    mu4[t] <- epsilon[t]+temp*(x_4[t-1]-epsilon[t-1]);
    mu5[t] <- epsilon[t]+temp*(x_5[t-1]-epsilon[t-1]);
  }
  Sigma1 <- Sigma_m-temp1;
  Sigma2 <- Sigma_m-temp1;
  Sigma3 <- Sigma_m-temp1;
  Sigma4 <- Sigma_m-temp1;
  Sigma5 <- Sigma_m-temp1;
  for (t in (cur-1):1)
  {
    mu1[t] <- epsilon[t]+temp*(x_1[t+1]-epsilon[t+1]);
    mu2[t] <- epsilon[t]+temp*(x_2[t+1]-epsilon[t+1]);
    mu3[t] <- epsilon[t]+temp*(x_3[t+1]-epsilon[t+1]);
    mu4[t] <- epsilon[t]+temp*(x_4[t+1]-epsilon[t+1]);
    mu5[t] <- epsilon[t]+temp*(x_5[t+1]-epsilon[t+1]);
  }
  for (t in 1:time)
  {
    xx_1[t] <- log(M_1*exp10(x_1[t]))/log(10); 
    xx_2[t] <- log(M_2*exp10(x_2[t]))/log(10);
    xx_3[t] <- log(M_3*exp10(x_3[t]))/log(10);
    xx_4[t] <- log(M_4*exp10(x_4[t]))/log(10);
    xx_5[t] <- log(M_5*exp10(x_5[t]))/log(10);
  }
}
model{
  diag_sigma ~ inv_gamma(sig_a,sig_b);
  increment_log_prob(lkj_corr_log(Rho,1)+priors(Rho,N,beta1,beta2));
    epsilon[cur] ~ normal(mu_m,mu_prior_var);
    x_1[cur] ~ multi_normal(epsilon[cur],Sigma_m);
    x_2[cur] ~ multi_normal(epsilon[cur],Sigma_m);
    x_3[cur] ~ multi_normal(epsilon[cur],Sigma_m);
    x_4[cur] ~ multi_normal(epsilon[cur],Sigma_m);
    x_5[cur] ~ multi_normal(epsilon[cur],Sigma_m);
    for (i in 1:N_1){
      y_1[i,cur] ~ multi_normal(xx_1[cur],Sigma_1);
    }
    for (i in 1:N_2){
      y_2[i,cur] ~ multi_normal(xx_2[cur],Sigma_2);
    }
    for (i in 1:N_3){
      y_3[i,cur] ~ multi_normal(xx_3[cur],Sigma_3);
    }
    for (i in 1:N_4){
      y_4[i,cur] ~ multi_normal(xx_4[cur],Sigma_4);
    }
    for (i in 1:N_5){
      y_5[i,cur] ~ multi_normal(xx_5[cur],Sigma_5);
    }
  for (t in (cur-1):1){
     epsilon[t] ~ multi_normal(epsilon[t+1],A);
     x_1[t] ~ multi_normal(mu1[t],Sigma1);
     x_2[t] ~ multi_normal(mu2[t],Sigma2);
     x_3[t] ~ multi_normal(mu3[t],Sigma3);
     x_4[t] ~ multi_normal(mu4[t],Sigma4);
     x_5[t] ~ multi_normal(mu5[t],Sigma5);
     for (i in 1:N_1){
       y_1[i,t] ~ multi_normal(xx_1[t],Sigma_1);
     }
     for (i in 1:N_2){
       y_2[i,t] ~ multi_normal(xx_2[t],Sigma_2);
     }
     for (i in 1:N_3){
       y_3[i,t] ~ multi_normal(xx_3[t],Sigma_3);
     }
     for (i in 1:N_4){
       y_4[i,t] ~ multi_normal(xx_4[t],Sigma_4);
     }
     for (i in 1:N_5){
       y_5[i,t] ~ multi_normal(xx_5[t],Sigma_5);
     }
  }
  for (t in cur+1:time){
     epsilon[t] ~ multi_normal(epsilon[t-1],A);
     x_1[t] ~ multi_normal(mu1[t],Sigma1);
     x_2[t] ~ multi_normal(mu2[t],Sigma2);
     x_3[t] ~ multi_normal(mu3[t],Sigma3);
     x_4[t] ~ multi_normal(mu4[t],Sigma4);
     x_5[t] ~ multi_normal(mu5[t],Sigma5);
     for (i in 1:N_1){
       y_1[i,t] ~ multi_normal(xx_1[t],Sigma_1);
     }
     for (i in 1:N_2){
       y_2[i,t] ~ multi_normal(xx_2[t],Sigma_2);
     }
     for (i in 1:N_3){
       y_3[i,t] ~ multi_normal(xx_3[t],Sigma_3);
     }
     for (i in 1:N_4){
       y_4[i,t] ~ multi_normal(xx_4[t],Sigma_4);
     }
     for (i in 1:N_5){
       y_5[i,t] ~ multi_normal(xx_5[t],Sigma_5);
     }
  }
}

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] IMK Stall detected

Most likely adaptation is kicking in and you're taking more
iterations than whatever is reporting the "stall" is expecting.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] IMK Stall detected
parts:
Thanks Bob

I tried to simplify my model down and build it up slowly. The problem went away until I added the parameter C (which is block covariance matrix for two time points). This parameter comes in here: 

I have some latent variables, x and mu (both are vectors with N elements), with joint distributions

(x[t],x[t+1])' ~ multiNorm((mu[t],mu[t+1])',COV)

where mu is at some higher level and COV is of the form

Sigma C'
C  Sigma

and then

x[t+1] ~ multiNorm(mu+C*inv(Sigma)*(x[t]-mu[t]),Sigma-C*inv(Sigma)*C')

When the model ran I got a lot of errors saying that the new covariance parameter ("Sigma-C*inv(Sigma)*C'" above) was not positive definite when trying to find initial points and it eventually gave up. When I set the initial values I got the message

IMK Stall detected, *please Report* your user scenario in <rdar://problem/16792073> - (imkxpc_windowLevelWithReply:) block performed very slowly (2.74 secs)

many times again. A better way to do this may be to be to specify the whole matrix in the parameters ie.

parameters{
  cov_matrix [2*N] COV;
...
}

and then specify that

COV[N+1:2*N,N+1:2*N] <- COV[1:N,1:N]

I tried this in the transform parameters part but the same thing as above seemed to happen. Is this possible and if so where do I do it? If this did happen, am I right in thinking that it would never converge as the algorithm would just be wandering round the COV[N+1:2*N,N+1:2*N] space. Can anyone think of a better way of defining the parameters as described above?

Cheers
Mike
